scope: Sargent and Stachurski, Dynamic Programming, Volume 2 (General States), Chapter 9: Approximation and Learning. Kernel averagers (9.2)-(9.3), nonexpansive and order preserving on bX (Lemmas 9.1.1, 9.1.6, Remark 9.1.2), Gaussian kernels and piecewise linear interpolation (Examples 9.1.1-9.1.2, with interpolation and uniqueness), least squares global approximation; fitted value iteration under Assumption 9.1.1 (Lemma 9.1.2, Theorems 9.1.3-9.1.4, Proposition 9.1.5, termination of Algorithm 9.1); damped iteration (Lemma 9.1.7, with convexity needed) and the asset pricing example (Exercise 9.1.1, unbiased sampling, the noise bounds); the Robbins-Siegmund lemma and the Robbins-Monro theorem (Theorem 9.1.8 for contractions of a real Hilbert space); asynchronous stochastic approximation for max-norm pseudo-contractions (Tsitsiklis, 1994), giving Theorem 9.1.8 in the supremum norm, Remark 9.1.3, almost sure convergence of the batch (9.15) and sequential (9.16) asset pricing updates, and Theorem 9.2.1 (convergence of Q-learning); Q-learning (the Q-factor operator, its fixed point, unbiased samples and the update (9.18)); risk-sensitive Q-learning as an order-reversing FDP (Exercises 9.2.1-9.2.2, (9.19), (9.22), Theorem 5.2.18); local-to-global optimality (Theorem 9.2.2, with irreducibility needed); with the earlier chapters' ADP, finite MDP, Q-factor and FDP theory restated.
source: Thomas J. Sargent and John Stachurski, Dynamic Programming, Volume 2: General States, Chapter 9, pp. 295-321.
